$comment: The vendoring manifest (AD-12, nave.pub#113). The design system is copy-vendored
by rule — apps inline it because they are no-build static clients — and until this
file existed, nothing could tell whether a copy was current. The cost was already
paid three ways: two token generations live in production (--panel2 vs --panel-2),
three apps lost their light theme purely because their copies were old, and every
titlebar provenance stamp in the fleet is stale while the bodies are current,
because the stamp was prose rather than a hash.
Check the fleet with:    node bin/nave-drift
A consumer may carry `root` when its clone is not a sibling of the hub — on the maintainer's Mac ngage and waggle live elsewhere. $HOME is expanded at run time so no absolute user path is stored.
`consumers` is also the source of the plane switcher's app list, so one file
drives both the drift check and the fleet navigation.

artifacts.note: Apps override ONLY --accent / --accent-bright / --accent-ink. A copy that differs in any other declaration is drift, not customisation.

consumers.note: bespoke letterpress-noir palette (gold/cream/ink), not a vendored copy — a deliberate design identity, same status as waggle. The one shared rule it DOES follow is the type system: chrome is --sans and only the signed artifact keeps --serif (DESIGN.md §Type).
private token block, not a vendored copy — adoption tracked in nave.pub#113

artifacts.note: Five different sibling lists exist across five copies today, and six surfaces carry no footer at all. Reconciling those is nave.pub#113 follow-up work, not a hash mismatch to silence.

apps.label: waggle
apps.note: lowercase always — never Waggle or WAGGLE
